summary: Follow-up of the accepted parent: direct analytic proof of Bloch's finite Fourier identity, with its Bernoulli horizontal term, logarithmic sum, dilogarithmic boundary cancellation and absolute convergence. The seven existing ER.4 declarations are imported by id. AC.0 alone owns general finite-abelian Fourier theory; ER.4 uses its already planned torsion coordinates. Constant-field trace is imported; geometric trace remains the explicitly identified ER.7 supplier gap.

sources.edition: Thesis, Paris 7, 2005; arXiv math/0602186v1, French, 155 pages.
readSections: §1.2, pp.20–28: Definitions 19, Remark 20, Theorem 21, Propositions 22,24,26 and their proofs. In particular Theorem 21 obtains its torsion expansion from Bloch 10.2.1, so it is not an input to the new direct proof.

nodes.title: Convergence for Bloch’s direct torsion calculation
nodes.statement: For every u∈T_C, the forward and backward raw logarithmic orbit series are absolutely summable after defining W(z)=log|z| log(1−z) with W(1)=0; both double logarithmic power series Σ_{n≥0,j≥1}log|x_u q^n|(x_u q^n)^j/j and Σ_{n≥1,j≥1}log|x_u^(−1)q^n|(x_u^(−1)q^n)^j/j are absolutely summable, with zero forward summands when n=ℓ=0; the corresponding Li₂ imaginary orbit series and the double power series Σ_{n≥0,j≥1}(x_u q^n)^j/j² and Σ_{n≥1,j≥1}(x_u^(−1)q^n)^j/j² are absolutely summable. For bounded periodic f, each of Σ_{m≠0,n} f(m,n)/(m(mτ+n)²), Σ_{m≠0,n} f(m,n) Im(1/(m²(mτ+n))), Σ'_{m,n} f(m,n)/((mτ+n)²(mτ̄+n)), and Σ_{n≠0}f(0,n)/n³ is absolutely summable. Here Σ' omits (0,0); Im is taken before multiplication by f.
hypotheses: C is a positive integer; τ∈ℍ, y=Im τ>0, q=exp(2πiτ).
T_C=(ℤ/C)²; u=(k,ℓ) uses canonical representatives 0≤k,ℓ<C; x_u=exp(2πi(k+ℓτ)/C).
f:T_C→ℂ, extended periodically to ℤ². f̂(k,ℓ)=C^(−2)Σ_{a,b}f(a,b)exp(2πi(−ak+bℓ)/C). No reality assumption.
proofSteps: Use norm_qParam: |q|<1, |x_u|≤1 and |x_u^(−1)q|<1. The only forward boundary is n=ℓ=0. There W vanishes because log|x_u|=0, including x_u=1. For the tail, |log(1−z)|≤A|z| from the principal logarithm Taylor series; |log|x_u q^n|| grows linearly, so n|q|^n dominates the log orbit series. Before exchanging the logarithmic n,j sums, bound Σ_{j≥1}|z|^j/j≤|z|/(1−|z|) on |z|<1. Away from the zero-weight forward boundary, the orbit moduli have a common upper bound r<1; multiplying this bound by |log|z|| gives O((n+1)|q|^n). At n=ℓ=0 every weighted power-series summand is exactly zero. This proves absolute convergence of both logarithmic double series, not just of their orbit sums.

On the closed unit disc, Li₂ equals Σ_{j≥1} z^j/j²: import P.1 continuity and its open-disc series, extend by uniform 1/j² domination. For n≥1 the sum of absolute values is bounded by A|q|^n; for n=0 use the convergent p=2 series. This proves the absolute double-series bounds needed to exchange n,j and finite character sums.

For a=|m|y>0, divide integers n into shells j≤|n+m Re τ|<j+1, at most four per shell. Comparison with the integral of (a²+t²)^(−1) gives Σ_n|mτ+n|^(−2)≤K_y/|m|. Hence the log-kernel norm sum is ≤K_yΣ_{m≠0}|m|^(−2). The projected imaginary kernel has absolute value y/(|m||mτ+n|²), so the same bound applies. Do not claim the unprojected reciprocal series is absolutely summable.

For the full cubic kernel, the real-linear map (m,n)↦mτ+n is invertible because y>0. Its lower norm bound and EisensteinSeries.summable_one_div_norm_rpow at k=3 give the result. The horizontal series uses p=3. Boundedness of f follows from finiteness of T_C.

sources.locator: §10.3, pp.80–85, sum rearrangements underlying (10.3.2) and Propositions 10.3.1,10.3.3
sources.match: The source rearranges the logarithmic double series in (10.3.3) on p.81 and the Li₂ double series in the proof of Proposition 10.3.3 on pp.82–84. These are the supporting calculations, not a separately printed convergence theorem. The packet supplies the required orbit, double-series and lattice estimates independently, including the unit-circle exception.

acceptance: At ℓ=0 the logarithmic n=0 contribution is zero; the Li₂ n=0 contribution is retained.
All lattice identities use product-index absolute sums, not a silently chosen order of summation.
The row bound is uniform in the translate m Re τ; no irrationality condition on Re τ.
The logarithmic Taylor expansion is interchanged with the orbit sum only after the weighted n,j norm sum is proved summable; the unit-circle zero-weight term is handled separately.

nodes.title: Bloch’s logarithmic term L
nodes.statement: Define blochLogTerm(C,τ,f)=L=Σ_{u∈T_C}f̂(u)A_τ(x_u), where W(z)=log|z| log(1−z), W(1)=0, and A_τ(x)=Σ_{n≥0}W(xq^n)−Σ_{n≥1}W(x^(−1)q^n). Complex.log is the principal logarithm; canonical torsion lifts make both tails lie in the closed unit disc. This construction is the weighted specialization of the raw regulator’s logarithmic part, not a new elliptic companion.
hypotheses: C is a positive integer; τ∈ℍ, y=Im τ>0, q=exp(2πiτ).
T_C=(ℤ/C)²; u=(k,ℓ) uses canonical representatives 0≤k,ℓ<C; x_u=exp(2πi(k+ℓτ)/C).
f:T_C→ℂ, extended periodically to ℤ². f̂(k,ℓ)=C^(−2)Σ_{a,b}f(a,b)exp(2πi(−ak+bℓ)/C). No reality assumption.
proofSteps: Use the imported torsion transform and q-parameter; define A only at canonical torsion lifts.
The convergence theorem gives both orbit sums; multiply by the finite Fourier coefficients and sum.
Complex linearity is in f, not in x. The raw part depends on its lift; it is not asserted q-invariant.

sources.match: In (10.3.2), L weights R′_q, the forward-minus-backward principal-complex-log expression immediately above it. The real logarithmic factor multiplies the full complex logarithm; it includes the argument term.

acceptance: Zero input gives zero on both sides.
C=1 or C=2 forces an odd complex-valued input to vanish.
Complex scalar multiplication preserves the identity; no coefficient passes through Im.

api.name: blochLogTerm_character
api.statement: For χ_u(a,b)=ZMod.stdAddChar(ak−bℓ), L(C,τ,χ_u)=A_τ(x_u), by AC.0 character orthogonality and the imported torsion identification.

api.name: blochLogTerm_boundary
api.statement: For |z|=1, W(z)=0, including z=1. This is an equality for the weighted summand, not a Taylor series assertion for log(1−z).

uses.how: Rewriting L with weighted geometric series isolates the logarithmic lattice kernel.

uses.where: Direct raw Fourier identity in this packet
uses.how: Adds to the independently computed dilogarithmic contribution.

tests.name: log_test_trivial_level
tests.statement: At C=1, L(1,τ,f)=0 for every f (A_τ(1)=0 by tail cancellation).

tests.name: log_test_character_level_three
tests.statement: For C=3 and u=(0,1), L(3,τ,χ_u)=A_τ(exp(2πiτ/3)); no factor 3 or 9.

tests.name: log_test_unit_boundary
tests.statement: W(i)=W(1)=0, although log(1−i) is nonzero; only the weighted summand is erased.

tests.name: log_test_complex_scalar
tests.statement: L(C,τ,i f)=i L(C,τ,f). This tests complex linearity in the coefficient function; a real-part logarithmic kernel also passes it.

tests.name: log_test_nonreal_kernel
tests.statement: Im W(i/2)=log(2) arctan(1/2)>0. Replacing Complex.log(1−z) by log|1−z| makes the left side zero, so this test detects loss of the logarithmic argument contribution to the regulator.

nodes.title: Bloch’s dilogarithmic term M
nodes.statement: Define blochDilogTerm(C,τ,f)=M=i Σ_{u∈T_C}f̂(u)V_τ(x_u), where V_τ(x)=Σ_{n≥0}Im Li₂(xq^n)−Σ_{n≥1}Im Li₂(x^(−1)q^n). On |z|≤1 use P.1’s principal Li₂, equal to the absolutely convergent Σ_{j≥1}z^j/j². Im is applied to each Li₂ value before the complex Fourier coefficient. Together A_τ(x)+iV_τ(x)=R_q^{Bl}(x)=J_q^{Bl}(x)+iD_q(x); the log|z| arg(1−z) part of D is in A, so V alone is not D_q.
hypotheses: C is a positive integer; τ∈ℍ, y=Im τ>0, q=exp(2πiτ).
T_C=(ℤ/C)²; u=(k,ℓ) uses canonical representatives 0≤k,ℓ<C; x_u=exp(2πi(k+ℓτ)/C).
f:T_C→ℂ, extended periodically to ℤ². f̂(k,ℓ)=C^(−2)Σ_{a,b}f(a,b)exp(2πi(−ak+bℓ)/C). No reality assumption.
proofSteps: Use imported P.1 Li₂ with its closed-disc continuity; the series coordinate form follows by uniform p=2 domination.
Form the two absolutely summable imaginary orbit sums, then the finite complex-linear weighted sum.
Expand the definition of D(z)=Im Li₂(z)+log|z|arg(1−z) and of J; principal log identifies A+iV with the imported raw Bloch regulator.

sources.match: In (10.3.2), M=−iΣ f̂ R″_q; the integral defining R″_q is the negative of the principal Li₂ value. Thus the packet has +i times the forward-minus-backward imaginary Li₂ sums. Projection occurs before the Fourier coefficient.

acceptance: Zero input gives zero on both sides.
C=1 or C=2 forces an odd complex-valued input to vanish.
Complex scalar multiplication preserves the identity; no coefficient passes through Im.

api.name: blochDilogTerm_smul
api.statement: M(C,τ,c f)=c M(C,τ,f) for all complex c.

api.name: blochDilogTerm_character
api.statement: M(C,τ,χ_u)=i V_τ(x_u), using the same torsion character as L.

api.name: blochDilogTerm_split
api.statement: For odd f, M=M₁+M₂, where M₁=2iΣ_u f̂(u)Im Σ_{n≥0}Li₂(x_u q^n), M₂=−iΣ_k f̂(k,0)Im Li₂(exp(2πik/C)); both sums converge absolutely. The ℓ=0 boundary survives the orbit reindexing.

uses.how: M₁ carries a cotangent sum and an extra H term; M₂ removes H.

uses.where: Raw Fourier identity; ER.3 companion comparison
uses.how: The imaginary Li₂ piece combines with the principal-log piece to give R^{Bl}, rather than the dilogarithm alone.

tests.name: dilog_test_character_level_three
tests.statement: M(3,τ,χ_(0,1))=i V_τ(exp(2πiτ/3)); the character test catches the Fourier sign and C^(−2) factor.

tests.name: dilog_test_complex_scalar
tests.statement: M(C,τ,i f)=i M(C,τ,f); Im must not be moved outside a complex-weighted sum.

tests.name: dilog_test_unit_circle
tests.statement: For C=4, τ=i and χ_(1,0), M=i Im Li₂(i)+2iΣ_{n≥1}Im Li₂(i exp(−2πn)); the nonzero unit-circle Li₂ value is retained.

nodes.title: Splitting the dilogarithmic orbit sum
nodes.statement: blochDilogTerm_split: for odd f, M=M₁+M₂, where M₁=2iΣ_u f̂(u)Im Σ_{n≥0}Li₂(x_u q^n) and M₂=−iΣ_k f̂(k,0)Im Li₂(exp(2πik/C)). This promotes the definition’s relation API to the explicit prerequisite used by the lattice evaluation.
hypotheses: C is a positive integer; τ∈ℍ, y=Im τ>0, q=exp(2πiτ).
T_C=(ℤ/C)²; u=(k,ℓ) uses canonical representatives 0≤k,ℓ<C; x_u=exp(2πi(k+ℓτ)/C).
f:T_C→ℂ, extended periodically to ℤ². f̂(k,ℓ)=C^(−2)Σ_{a,b}f(a,b)exp(2πi(−ak+bℓ)/C). No reality assumption.
f(−u)=−f(u) for all u∈T_C; consequently f(0)=0 and f̂ is odd.
proofSteps: Change u to −u in the backward sum and use f̂(−u)=−f̂(u). For ℓ>0, the canonical negative lift is q/x_u, so n≥1 becomes n−1≥0.
For ℓ=0 the canonical negative lift is 1/x_u; the backward series becomes the forward one with its n=0 term omitted.
The finite weighted sum is thus twice the forward sum minus exactly the ℓ=0 endpoint. Absolute convergence justifies the reindexing and taking Im termwise.

sources.locator: (10.3.2) and decomposition in proof of Proposition 10.3.3, pp.80,82–83
sources.match: The proof of Proposition 10.3.3 consolidates the backward sum by negating the torsion index, then splits M into M₁+M₂. The ℓ=0, n=0 endpoint occurs once with coefficient −i.

acceptance: The ℓ=0 boundary is retained with coefficient −i, not −2i.
Complex f is permitted; only the real Li₂ values are projected.

nodes.title: The Bernoulli horizontal term
nodes.statement: Let b_τ(u)=4π²y²(t³/3−t²/2+t/6), t=ℓ/C. Then B=Σ_u f̂(u)b_τ(u)=(iy²/π)Σ_{n≠0}f(0,n)/n³. This is the unscaled correction for the analytic R_q, before multiplying by C³ for the K₂ classes.
hypotheses: C is a positive integer; τ∈ℍ, y=Im τ>0, q=exp(2πiτ).
T_C=(ℤ/C)²; u=(k,ℓ) uses canonical representatives 0≤k,ℓ<C; x_u=exp(2πi(k+ℓτ)/C).
f:T_C→ℂ, extended periodically to ℤ². f̂(k,ℓ)=C^(−2)Σ_{a,b}f(a,b)exp(2πi(−ak+bℓ)/C). No reality assumption.
f(−u)=−f(u) for all u∈T_C; consequently f(0)=0 and f̂ is odd.
proofSteps: Specialize Mathlib’s sine/Bernoulli formula at k=1. Pair ±n to obtain Σ_{n≠0}exp(2πint)/n³=(4π³i/3)B₃(t), including endpoints 0,1.
Multiply by −iy²/π and exchange the absolutely convergent n sum with the finite u sum.
AC.0 inversion in the imported ER.4 coordinates gives Σ_u f̂(u)exp(2πinℓ/C)=f(0,−n). Oddness changes the minus sign to plus.

sources.match: Lemma 10.2.3 states the horizontal n^(−3) identity. Its proof uses the cubic Bernoulli Fourier series, inverse transform at (0,−n), and oddness to obtain the positive iy²/π factor. Capital C follows inherited E11.

acceptance: For C=3 and f=δ_(0,1)−δ_(0,2), B=8π²i y²/(81√3); the horizontal row has that value after multiplying by iy²/π.
The inherited capital-C correction is source issue EllipticRegulators/E11; no new spelling of it is introduced.
For an input supported off the row a=0 the correction vanishes.

nodes.title: Evaluation of Bloch’s logarithmic term
nodes.statement: L=−y/(2π) Σ_{m≠0,n∈ℤ} f(m,n)/(m(mτ+n)²). All indices are signed integers; the m=0 row is absent.
hypotheses: C is a positive integer; τ∈ℍ, y=Im τ>0, q=exp(2πiτ).
T_C=(ℤ/C)²; u=(k,ℓ) uses canonical representatives 0≤k,ℓ<C; x_u=exp(2πi(k+ℓτ)/C).
f:T_C→ℂ, extended periodically to ℤ². f̂(k,ℓ)=C^(−2)Σ_{a,b}f(a,b)exp(2πi(−ak+bℓ)/C). No reality assumption.
f(−u)=−f(u) for all u∈T_C; consequently f(0)=0 and f̂ is odd.
proofSteps: Use oddness of f̂ to combine the forward/backward log orbit sums. The ℓ=0 endpoint has multiplier n+ℓ/C=0 at n=0; it contributes zero.

Expand the principal log only on the open unit-disc terms, using Complex.hasSum_taylorSeries_neg_log. Character orthogonality imposes j≡a (mod C); reindex nC+ℓ. The resulting expression is (4πy/C²)Σ_{a,b,j>0,j≡a} f(a,b)j^(−1)Σ_{r≥0}r exp(2πir(jτ+b)/C).
The weighted geometric baseline gives −1/(4sin²(πz)). The k=1 cotangent derivative gives π²/sin²(πz)=Σ_n(z+n)^(−2). Scale z=(jτ+b)/C and reindex b+Cn.

The positive j expression is −y/π times its positive-m lattice sum. Pair (m,n) with (−m,−n); both f and m change sign, so bilateralization introduces the factor 1/2. Convergence permits all rearrangements.

sources.match: Proposition 10.3.1 has −y/(2π), m≠0, and denominator m(mτ+n)². Its proof passes through (10.3.3) and the weighted geometric identity in Lemma 10.3.2; the latter is already supplied by the pinned Mathlib baseline.

acceptance: Zero input gives zero on both sides.
C=1 or C=2 forces an odd complex-valued input to vanish.
Complex scalar multiplication preserves the identity; no coefficient passes through Im.

nodes.title: Evaluation of the forward dilogarithmic sum
nodes.statement: For odd f define H=(1/C)Σ_{m≥1}Σ_{b mod C}f(m,b)/m² and M₁=2iΣ_u f̂(u)Im Σ_{n≥0}Li₂(x_u q^n). Then M₁=H−(1/(2π))Σ_{m≠0,n} f(m,n)Im(1/(m²(mτ+n))). These expressions are absolutely convergent.
hypotheses: C is a positive integer; τ∈ℍ, y=Im τ>0, q=exp(2πiτ).
T_C=(ℤ/C)²; u=(k,ℓ) uses canonical representatives 0≤k,ℓ<C; x_u=exp(2πi(k+ℓτ)/C).
f:T_C→ℂ, extended periodically to ℤ². f̂(k,ℓ)=C^(−2)Σ_{a,b}f(a,b)exp(2πi(−ak+bℓ)/C). No reality assumption.
f(−u)=−f(u) for all u∈T_C; consequently f(0)=0 and f̂ is odd.
proofSteps: Expand Li₂ on the closed disc and exchange the absolutely convergent sums. To handle complex f, pair (a,b) with (−a,−b): Σ f(a,b)Re(exp(2πi(−ak+bℓ)/C))=0. This identity, not moving complex scalars through Im, changes the remaining phase expression into f(a,b) times Im(i times the power series).
Sum over k to impose m≡a mod C and combine ℓ,n into a nonnegative integer r. Sum the geometric series with z=(mτ+b)/C (Im z>0).
Use 1/(1−exp(2πiz))=(1+i cotπz)/2. The constant 1/2 gives H. For the cotangent part use the paired baseline; its imaginary projection is absolutely summable, since Im 1/(mτ+n)=−my/|mτ+n|².
Reindex residue b+Cn and use simultaneous negation to convert the positive-m sum to half the bilateral sum.

sources.match: Lemma 10.3.4 evaluates M₁ with a positive H term and −1/(2π) times the projected reciprocal kernel. The proof uses oddness to remove the cosine phase, the geometric/cotangent identity, and paired cotangent partial fractions.

acceptance: Zero input gives zero on both sides.
C=1 or C=2 forces an odd complex-valued input to vanish.
Complex scalar multiplication preserves the identity; no coefficient passes through Im.

nodes.title: Cancellation of the unit-circle boundary
nodes.statement: For odd f, M₂=−iΣ_{k mod C}f̂(k,0)Im Li₂(exp(2πik/C))=−H, with H=(1/C)Σ_{m≥1,b mod C}f(m,b)/m². This cancels precisely the H in the forward evaluation.
